saml.description: Vault SAML auth does not validate response or assertion signatures unless explicitly enabled in auth config.
saml.note: A successful forged SAML login under default config is an insecure default/hardening finding, not evidence that Vault ignored explicitly enabled validation.

saml.description: Vault-issued bearer tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry or revocation.
saml.note: Replay of the same unexpired Vault bearer token is normal unless a nonzero use limit was configured.

saml.description: A token use limit of 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses.
saml.note: Do not flag repeated use of such tokens as a freshness violation.

saml.description: JWT nbf enforcement is optional per RFC 7519 and absence of nbf checking is spec-compliant.
saml.note: Do not treat acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf as a vulnerability by itself.

saml.description: Token lookup-self display_name may include the auth mount path as a prefix before the upstream username or alias.
saml.note: Prefix differences alone are not identity-collision bugs; compare the suffix/user component.

saml.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, causing shared privileges, if administrators create non-unique aliases.
saml.source: Vault identity entity-alias API important note on alias cardinality and alias reuse
saml.note: This is an admin-created identity modeling hazard documented by Vault, not an automatic broker merge bug.

saml.description: Vault identity alias names can be reused and multiple authenticated entities can bind to the same alias, causing privilege sharing.
saml.note: This is a documented identity-model risk and must be considered when interpreting collision results or when pre-seeding aliases.

saml.description: Admin changes to SAML IdP metadata URL, certificate, issuer/entity ID, or signature-validation settings take effect by design for subsequent logins.
saml.note: Do not flag acceptance under the new admin-configured trust anchor as a trust-substitution bug; only flag stale acceptance of the old trust after intended hardening/rotation semantics are violated.

saml.description: When group_policy_application_mode is set to 'any', identity group policies apply across namespace boundaries rather than only within the namespace hierarchy.
saml.note: Cross-namespace group policy reach is an explicit admin-selected mode, not unintended privilege escalation.

saml.description: Admin updates to policies or auth role configuration take effect immediately and legitimately change subsequent authorization outcomes.
saml.source: sys/policy API docs; auth/saml role docs
saml.note: Do not flag behavior changes caused by explicit admin reconfiguration as flow-coherence violations.

saml.constraint: SAML signature validation is opt-in. In /v1/auth/{mount}/config, validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 signature-integrity tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control these flags. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false; to test hardened behavior, set both true. Do NOT assume Vault validates any SAML signature by default.

Issuer validation depends on configuration source. If idp_metadata_url is used, the IdP entity ID comes from metadata. If manual configuration is used instead, idp_entity_id is required alongside idp_sso_url and idp_cert. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST configure a trusted issuer via metadata or explicit idp_entity_id; otherwise issuer comparison may be absent or undefined and results are not meaningful.

The SAML login flow is multi-step and session-bound: /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url returns token_poll_id and establishes RelayState/flow context, /v1/auth/{mount}/callback consumes the SAMLResponse, and /v1/auth/{mount}/token exchanges token_poll_id plus client_verifier for the Vault token. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep token_poll_id, client_verifier/client_challenge, RelayState, and callback/token exchange within the same flow. Mixing artifacts across flows will cause legitimate failures unrelated to security invariants.

The SSO bootstrap requires client_challenge to be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier, and client_challenge must be at least 44 bytes. The fuzzer MUST generate a matching verifier/challenge pair for every SAML flow; otherwise /v1/auth/{mount}/token failure is expected and not evidence of a security control.

The acs_url supplied to /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url MUST be one of the configured acs_urls on /v1/auth/{mount}/config. Using any other ACS URL will fail by design and must not be interpreted as an invariant violation.

Role selection semantics matter for I3 tests. If /v1/auth/{mount}/config.default_role is unset, login flows require an explicit role. If default_role is set, omitting role in the SSO bootstrap uses that default. For config-change tests involving role binding, the fuzzer MUST control whether role is explicit or inherited from default_role; otherwise behavior changes may be due to default-role selection rather than stale or incoherent evaluation.

bound_subjects matching is controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only; wildcards like * are literal characters. If bound_subjects_type=glob, * wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Do NOT set bound_subjects='*' under string mode expecting wildcard behavior.

bound_attributes matching is controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values are exact string matches only; wildcard characters are literal. In glob mode, * wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple attribute values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST omit the exact-match attribute constraint or explicitly set bound_attributes_type=glob with a deliberate pattern. Do NOT use '*' under the default string mode.

bound_attributes values are documented as single strings or comma-separated lists of strings, and authentication succeeds if the SAML attribute matches at least one expected value. For I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST treat these as string comparisons, not numeric/boolean typed comparisons. Numeric coercion attacks applicable to JWT claim binders are not directly supported by this SAML role parameter.

token_num_uses is a use-budget limiter on tokens issued by the SAML role. Value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Every API call made with the session token consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Therefore, if the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read verification, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-backed calls occur. Setting token_num_uses=1 will cause the verification step to exhaust the token before the access test.

Vault token and TTL sentinel semantics are non-obvious. In SAML role reads, token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 do not mean immediate expiry; they mean unset/default behavior inherited from system or mount settings. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret 0 as literal zero lifetime for these fields.

KV v2 engine config has sentinel values with special meaning. max_versions=0 means use the platform default of 10 versions, not keep zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST account for both sentinels when setting up protected resources and freshness-related tests.

For KV v2 access tests, the read path MUST include /data/: use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Listing uses /metadata and writes use /data. Omitting /data on a KV v2 mount hits the wrong API shape and yields false failures.

Vault policy creation documentation here uses the legacy /v1/sys/policy/{name} endpoint. The fuzzer should use exactly the documented path from this corpus for this profile; do not assume the newer ACL policy endpoint unless separately documented for the target extraction set.

Identity group aliases require the auth mount accessor, not the mount path. The fuzzer MUST obtain the accessor from /v1/sys/auth and pass it as mount_accessor when creating /v1/identity/group-alias. Using the mount path string instead will not bind external SAML groups correctly.

External group mapping for SAML is alias-based. groups_attribute on the SAML role causes successful logins to create/use Identity group aliases named from the SAML attribute values. For I5 group-policy escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST pre-create internal groups and matching group aliases; merely setting groups_attribute without alias setup will not attach the intended internal group policies.

Identity alias reuse is a documented security concern in Vault. Alias names are not inherently unique across principals, and multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias if configured that way. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST treat alias cardinality and mount accessor as part of the binding surface and avoid pre-seeding aliases that would collapse distinct principals unless that collapse is the behavior under test.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as expired assertions, the sequence MUST include a control flow using a valid assertion first. Otherwise, a failed expired-assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup, bad ACS URL, bad verifier/challenge pairing, or missing role/default_role configuration.

For I2 replay tests on SAML assertions, replay must be tested against the same logical assertion/flow artifacts as required by the platform. Because Vault uses a multi-step SAML flow with callback plus token polling, the fuzzer MUST preserve the intended replay dimensions carefully: same assertion ID for assertion replay, same OneTimeUse condition for OneTimeUse replay, and valid flow context for each submission. Failures caused by mismatched RelayState or token_poll_id are not replay protections.

For I1 saml_spurious_signature and unsigned-assertion tests, validate_response_signature and validate_assertion_signature are independent toggles. The fuzzer MUST test combinations intentionally: response-only validation may still accept an unsigned assertion by design if assertion validation is disabled; assertion-level integrity requires validate_assertion_signature=true.

Group policy application can be globally widened by /v1/sys/config/group-policy-application. Default mode within_namespace_hierarchy restricts identity-group policy application by namespace hierarchy; mode any applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. For I5 group-policy escalation tests in Enterprise/multi-namespace setups, the fuzzer MUST record this global mode because cross-namespace policy reach may be by-design under mode=any.

SAML signature validation is opt-in in Vault SAML auth config: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 signature-integrity tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set these fields according to the test objective. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false; to test enforcement, enable the relevant flag(s).

Vault SAML IdP trust can be configured either by idp_metadata_url OR by the explicit triple idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. These modes are mutually exclusive. For I1 issuer/trust-anchor tests that need a fixed trusted issuer/cert, the fuzzer SHOULD prefer explicit idp_entity_id and idp_cert rather than metadata URL so the expected issuer and certificate are pinned in config.

If default_role is not configured on /auth/{mount}/config, a role is required during SAML login flow startup. The fuzzer MUST either set default_role during auth config or ensure the login flow is initiated with an explicit role before posting the SAMLResponse.

SAML login in Vault is a multi-step flow bound by client_challenge/client_verifier and token_poll_id: start at /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url, complete /auth/{mount}/callback, then exchange at /auth/{mount}/token. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep token_poll_id, RelayState/InResponseTo, and client_verifier from the SAME flow instance. Mixing artifacts across flows will fail by design and is not a vulnerability.

For saml_login, the ACS URL used in the flow must be one of the configured acs_urls. The fuzzer MUST initiate the flow with an acs_url that exactly matches a configured ACS URL; otherwise callback validation failure is expected and not security-relevant.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, * wildcards are supported. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT set bound_subjects='*' unless bound_subjects_type is also set to glob; with string matching, '*' is treated literally. If multiple different subjects must authenticate to the same role, omit bound_subjects entirely or use glob mode intentionally.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values must match exactly; in glob mode, * wildcards are supported. For I4/I5 tests requiring multiple different attribute values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit the exact-match constraint or set bound_attributes_type=glob explicitly. Do NOT assume '*' works under the default string mode.

bound_attributes values are documented as either a single string or a comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if at least one expected value matches. For I5 claim/attribute type-coercion tests, Vault SAML docs do not specify non-string cross-type behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD test whether non-string attribute values are rejected outright versus coerced, but MUST expect documented matching semantics to be string-oriented.

groups_attribute controls which SAML attribute values become Identity group alias names on successful login. Group policy effects therefore depend on pre-created identity groups and group aliases with the correct mount_accessor. For I5 group-policy tests, the fuzzer MUST create the identity group and matching group alias before login; otherwise missing group-derived policies are expected setup failure, not an authorization bug.

token_num_uses on the SAML role is a session-use budget. Every API call made with the resulting Vault token consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence includes both a self-lookup and a protected-resource read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are present. Setting token_num_uses=1 will cause the access test to fail for budget exhaustion, not authorization.
Numeric sentinel semantics on SAML role token settings: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as 'no limit' when reasoning about replay/use-budget tests.

Numeric sentinel semantics on SAML role token TTL fields as returned by read_role_config: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than literal immediate expiry. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret returned 0 values as 'expired now' without corroborating token lookup data.

KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means Vault keeps 10 versions by default, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST account for both sentinels when designing freshness or storage-retention tests.

KV v2 CAS semantics: when cas_required is enabled, writes must include options.cas. cas=0 means create only if the key does not yet exist; for existing or soft-deleted keys, cas must match the current version. The fuzzer MUST use the correct CAS mode when reseeding protected resources mid-sequence, or write failures will be by design.

For verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2, the read path MUST include /data/ (/{engine}/data/{path}). Using the mount root path without /data/ targets the wrong API shape and will fail independently of authorization.

Vault token lookup-self returns display_name and metadata derived from the auth path and login metadata, not necessarily the raw upstream SAML subject. For I4 identity-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST compare entity_id and alias/entity records in addition to display_name, and should tolerate mount-prefixed display names.

Vault identity alias reuse is security-sensitive by design: documentation warns that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby share privileges. For I4 collision tests involving aliases, the fuzzer MUST create unique alias names per entity unless it is intentionally testing alias-collision behavior.

Vault identity entity merges are administrative operations that can collapse identities intentionally. For I4 tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT use /identity/entity/merge or pre-merged entities in the test environment, or identity collapse will be admin-authorized behavior rather than a broker flaw.

External identity groups in Vault are typically populated through group aliases from auth methods. For SAML group-mapping tests, the fuzzer SHOULD use create_identity_group with type='external' plus create_group_alias rather than relying on manual member_entity_ids to simulate upstream group membership.

For I2 SAML expiry tests, include a control login through the same configured flow before sending an expired assertion. Without a successful control flow, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup (ACS URL, role, RelayState, or trust config).

For I1 issuer-mismatch tests, if idp_entity_id is omitted because idp_metadata_url mode is used, issuer expectations come from metadata rather than an explicit config field. To test whether issuer validation is skipped when unset, configure via explicit fields and intentionally omit idp_entity_id only when the API allows that mode; otherwise metadata-driven issuer checks may confound the result.

Vault SAML callback behavior differs by client_type during flow initiation (cli returns HTML success page, browser returns blank HTML page), but token issuance still occurs via /auth/{mount}/token. The fuzzer MUST judge login success by the token endpoint result, not by callback body shape or HTML content.

SAML signature validation is opt-in in Vault SAML config: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 signature-integrity tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set these booleans according to the scenario. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false; to test enforcement, enable the relevant flag(s).

Issuer validation can be skipped if idp_metadata_url is used without an explicit idp_entity_id, or if manual configuration omits idp_entity_id. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST configure a trusted IdP entity ID and compare against a mismatched assertion Issuer. If idp_entity_id is left unset in manual config, acceptance may be by design because issuer binding was never configured.

SAML login is a 3-step flow bound by token_poll_id/client_verifier: first POST /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url, then POST /auth/{mount}/callback, then POST /auth/{mount}/token. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep token_poll_id, client_challenge, client_verifier, RelayState, and callback/token exchange within the same flow instance; mixing artifacts across flows will cause legitimate failures unrelated to security.

The ACS callback /auth/{mount}/callback does not itself return the Vault bearer token. The usable session token is only returned by /auth/{mount}/token. The fuzzer MUST treat callback success as an intermediate step and MUST use exchange_code_for_token before any session inspection or access test.

Role matching semantics: bound_subjects supports two modes controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only; if bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcards are honored. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring multiple different subjects to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an appropriate pattern. Do NOT set bound_subjects='*' while leaving type unset/string, because that matches only the literal '*'.

Attribute matching semantics: bound_attributes supports exact matching by default because bound_attributes_type defaults to string. Only bound_attributes_type=glob enables wildcard matching. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring multiple different attribute values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST omit the exact-match attribute constraint or explicitly set bound_attributes_type=glob with a suitable pattern. Do NOT assume '*' is a wildcard under the default string mode.

bound_attributes values are documented as a single string or comma-separated list of strings. Vault authenticates if the SAML attributes match at least one expected value. For I5 value-type tests, these are string comparisons; non-string typed claim/coercion scenarios are not documented for SAML attributes here, so the fuzzer SHOULD not assume numeric/boolean coercion support on bound_attributes.

token_num_uses limits how many API calls a Vault token can make, and every authenticated API call consumes uses, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. For sequences that perform both self-lookup and secret-read verification, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use a higher value if additional session-authenticated calls occur.
Numeric sentinel semantics for token_num_uses: value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'deny all' or single-use.

Numeric sentinel semantics for token TTL fields in SAML role reads: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 indicate unset/default/no explicit limit behavior rather than an immediately expired token. The fuzzer MUST not assume zero means literal zero lifetime.

KV v2 sentinel semantics: engine config max_versions=0 means Vault keeps the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. Never assume these zero values disable access or force instant expiry.
For I5 access tests against KV v2 mounts, the read path MUST include /data/ (e.g. /v1/{engine}/data/{path}). Using /v1/{engine}/{path} is KV v1 and will produce false 404s on KV v2 mounts.

KV v2 listing uses /metadata/ paths, not /data/. If the fuzzer seeds or verifies against KV v2 and also needs list capability, policies must grant list on /metadata/ even when reads/writes use /data/.

Vault SAML groups are mapped from the role's groups_attribute into Identity group aliases. To test group-based authorization (I5), the fuzzer MUST create an external identity group and a group alias whose name exactly matches the SAML attribute value emitted by the IdP for groups_attribute, using the SAML auth mount accessor. Manual member_entity_ids on the external group are not the SAML mapping mechanism.

Identity group type matters for federated groups. When modeling upstream SAML groups, the fuzzer SHOULD create the identity group as type='external' and attach policies there, then map the upstream group name via create_group_alias. Using internal groups with manual membership can mis-model SAML group grants.

Login enforcement requires at least one target selector among auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids, or identity_entity_ids. For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, the fuzzer MUST scope MFA enforcement to the SAML auth mount accessor or auth_method_types including the relevant method; otherwise the enforcement object is invalid and setup fails.

Vault MFA methods and login enforcements are namespace-aware. In community/root-namespace setups everything is in root, but in enterprise namespaces the fuzzer MUST create and test MFA resources in the same namespace as the SAML auth mount and identities to avoid false negatives.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a control flow using a valid assertion first. A failed expired-assertion login without a successful control cannot distinguish correct expiry enforcement from broken SAML setup.

For I2 replay tests such as saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, the fuzzer MUST reuse the same fixed_assertion_id across two otherwise valid SAML login attempts against the same configured provider/role. Changing other flow artifacts can turn the test into a generic invalid-request failure instead of a replay check.

Vault policy updates take effect immediately for associated users and tokens on subsequent authorization checks. For I3 config-change tests, a new access result after admin policy or role modification is by design; the fuzzer must show inconsistent handling of the same security-relevant artifact, not merely that an admin-authorized change altered behavior.
